readiness_assessment.reasoning: BOZ-02A (paleoclimate & pastoral adaptation) contains solid paleoclimate data (lake cores) but exhibits problematic climate determinism throughout. Faz C correctly red-flagged: Correlation ≠ causation risk is significant, especially claims C-B2-007 (seasonal hierarchy hypothesis) and C-B2-008 (climate-conflict causation). Modern archaeological consensus (2010s+) rejects environmental determinism in favor of multi-causal models. Section requires extensive language revision to reflect current historiographic consensus, NOT reduction in evidence. Material is salvageable but requires careful production framing.
qualifications: C-B2-002: 'Critical for promoting expansion' overstates determinism — climate was enabling condition, not determinant
C-B2-004: Single-region (Xinjiang) generalization — note geographic limitation
C-B2-005: Speculative trade-route causal link — separate hypothesis from documented hydroclimatic change
C-B2-007: Seasonal hierarchy is theoretical model, not documented mechanism — alternative explanations (warfare, prestige goods) equally plausible

C-B2-008 (CRITICAL): Climate-conflict causation is major historiographic error per modern archaeology — must explicitly present as 'contemporaneous correlation, causation debated' not 'climate deterioration caused conflict'
